# Changing Color Scheme in Hugo Scroll Theme (2025-01-14 21:31Z)

_**User**_

I'm looking to change the color scheme of this theme. Can you tell me where I can access those settings?

---

_**Assistant**_

Based on the provided code, the color scheme settings for the Hugo Scroll theme can be found in the CSS variables file:


```1:48:themes/hugo-scroll/assets/css/variables.scss
:root {

    /* === Cover / Landing area === */
    --cover-text-color: #37501a;
    /* Used for Landing screen menu buttons, but potentially usable for highlighting other things */
    --highlight: #86c440;
    --highlight-contrast: var(--cover-text-color);
    /*inverse colors used for :hover */
    --highlight-inverse: var(--cover-text-color);
    --highlight-inverse-contrast: white;

    /* visual guard around title and description, when the feature is enabled */
    --cover-title-and-description-guard-bg-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.6);
    --cover-title-text-shadow: white 0px 0px 7px;


    /* === sticky top/left navigation menus === */
    --sticky-menu-text-color: #9fd067;


    /* === Alternating content (post) sections  === */
    /* Light section - text color */
    --section-light-text-color: #3a4145;
    /* Light section - background color */
    --section-light-bg-color: #f2efe8;

    /* Dark section - text color */
    --section-dark-text-color: var(--section-light-bg-color);
    /* Dark section - background color */
    --section-dark-bg-color: #b80135;

    /* Light&Dark section >quote. Suppressive color, compared to 'Light section - text color'*/
    --section-uni-quote: grey;
    /* Light&Dark section `code` a bit darker than 'Light section - background color' */
    --section-uni-code-bg-color: #e0ded7;

    /* === Single pages=== */
    --single-page-text-color: var(--section-light-text-color);
    --single-page-bg-color: var(--section-light-bg-color);

    /* === Footer === */
    --footer-color-background: #22343a;
    --footer-color: #bbc7cc;

    /* === Lists === */
    /* define list element for unnumbered lists, leave empty for default list element */
    --ul-li-icon: fa-asterisk;
}
```


This file contains all the main color variables that control the theme's appearance. The key color variables you can modify are:

1. Cover/Landing area colors:
- `--cover-text-color`: Text color for the landing area
- `--highlight`: Color for menu buttons and highlights
- `--highlight-contrast`: Contrast color for highlighted elements

2. Section colors:
- `--section-light-text-color`: Text color for light sections
- `--section-light-bg-color`: Background color for light sections
- `--section-dark-text-color`: Text color for dark sections
- `--section-dark-bg-color`: Background color for dark sections

3. Footer colors:
- `--footer-color-background`: Footer background color
- `--footer-color`: Footer text color

To override these colors, you have two options:

1. Create or modify the `layouts/partials/custom_head.html` file and add your custom CSS:

```html
<style>
:root {
    --cover-text-color: #your-color !important;
    --highlight: #your-color !important;
    --section-dark-bg-color: #your-color !important;
    /* Add other color overrides as needed */
}
</style>
```

2. Directly modify the `themes/hugo-scroll/assets/css/variables.scss` file (note that this might make future theme updates more difficult)

The `!important` flag ensures your colors override the theme's default values.

Remember that the theme uses a light/dark alternating section pattern, so you'll want to ensure good contrast between your light and dark section colors.

>The image is being stretched because the object-fit property is set to fill. This causes the image to fill the entire container, distorting its aspect ratio. To maintain the aspect ratio, you can change the object-fit property to contain or cover.

contain will ensure the entire image is visible within the container, while maintaining its aspect ratio. It might leave some empty space within the container if the aspect ratios don't match.

cover will fill the entire container with the image, while maintaining its aspect ratio. It might clip parts of the image if the aspect ratios don't match.

Here's how you can fix it:

Using object-fit: contain: This will ensure the entire image is visible within the 800px by 100px container, maintaining its aspect ratio. There might be some empty space within the container if the image's aspect ratio is different.
Using object-fit: cover: This will fill the entire 800px by 100px container with the image, maintaining its aspect ratio. Parts of the image might be clipped if its aspect ratio is different.
Remove explicit width and height: If you want the image to be displayed with its intrinsic dimensions, you can remove the width and height properties. This will allow the image to scale naturally while maintaining its aspect ratio. However, you might need to adjust the container's dimensions to accommodate the image.
